ca_clearcut_boulder.blurb: Clearcut Boulder is a small bouldering spot in the Rock Creek drainage on the Eastern Sierra side near Mammoth Lakes, at roughly 8,500 feet. It marks the beginning of the talus that runs up toward the Gong Show Wall, so some climbers use it to loosen up. The thirteen problems cover almost the whole range, from a couple of VB and V0 lines through the middle grades to a handful of hard ones topping out around V9. Problems sit on south, east and north sides: the east side has shorter, powerful moves over a flat landing, the north side is longer and gentler, and the south side has uneven ground that needs careful pad placement. The walk in is short through forest.

ca_black_bluff_n_face_right_side.blurb: The right half of the Black Bluff north face sits in the San Bernardino Mountains above Big Bear Lake, around 7,200 feet. It is a long, mostly continuous cliff band that rises out of the pines and looks out over the surrounding country. Most of the thirteen climbs are single-pitch trad or alpine-style lines, running from 5.7 up to the low 5.12s, with plenty in the 5.10 range, plus a single easy boulder problem. The wall faces north. Cracks are the draw here. Reaching the cliff means a hike across a big flat plateau where the trail can be hard to follow, so going with someone who has been before or carrying a track is wise.

ca_grant_grove_boulder_problems.blurb: A small cluster of boulders near Grant Grove Village in Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Park, at about 6,600 feet, next to the paved Panoramic Point trail. Thirteen problems are listed, mostly boulder lines from VB through V3 with the bulk at V0 to V2, plus a few crack climbs rated 5.6 to 5.9 that can be done on trad gear or top rope. The setting has long views over Kings Canyon, and the boulders sit a short stroll past the lookout. It is a modest area, best as a quick session before or after other plans in the park rather than a destination in its own right. Bring a pad.

ca_area_b.blurb: Area B is the biggest sector of the Rainbow Boulders by the American River in Folsom, a couple of dozen yards southwest of Rainbow Bridge and only a little above sea level. Its centerpiece is one large boulder right beside the water, with thirteen problems on it from V1 up to V6. Expect steep, juggy movement and some exciting topouts, with a number of problems themed around eggs. Landings can be awkward: the ground drops away toward the river and is overgrown with poison oak and blackberry, so bring pads and spotters. The rest of the cluster is small granite boulders of roughly 8 to 15 feet.

ca_3rd_tier.blurb: The 3rd Tier is the highest of the three ledge systems that make up The Tiers, a cliff in Woodfords Canyon (Cloudburst Canyon) beside Highway 88 near Carson Pass, at about 6,600 feet. Routes begin from the third ledge. Nearly all are traditional pitches, with a lone sport line, and the grades cluster around 5.10 with a few climbs a notch easier and a few reaching 5.11. The wall sits directly west of the One of These Days wall, and the way up follows the trail from that wall, crossing the creek where you reach the right ledge. A good place for a climber comfortable leading the 5.10 range on gear.

ca_shadow_boulder.blurb: Shadow Boulder is one of the boulders in the Split Rock area of Donner Memorial State Park near Truckee, at roughly 5,950 feet, a short way south of the namesake split erratic. Mostly shaded, it suits warmer days. The thirteen problems begin with a couple of VB lines and several V0s, then move into a middle band around V2 to V5, with one much harder problem near V8. The best known are a V3 and a V4 dyno. Expect short sessions and a mellow, forested setting, easily combined with the other boulders around Split Rock.

ca_lower_irish_boulders.blurb: Lower Irish Boulders is a quiet bouldering sub-area of the Irish Boulders in the Conejo hills near Thousand Oaks and Newbury Park, at under 900 feet. Thirteen problems are mostly easy to moderate, from V0 to V3, with one much harder line near V7. It sits on the shadier side of the hill, so the landings and boulders grow over quickly, and poison oak is plentiful. Rattlesnakes are common except on the coldest days, and ticks show up in spring. The walk in is a steep, slippery drop, so brushes and good approach shoes help. Cooler months are the sensible time to visit.

ca_penstemon_dome_west_face.blurb: The West Face is the main side of Penstemon Dome, a granite dome of the Southern Sierra near Courtright Reservoir, high up at around 8,200 to 8,700 feet. It is the face visible from the parking area and holds most of the dome's routes: a mix of multi-pitch trad lines and bolted routes, with grades from 5.6 up to 5.12. Most of the thirteen climbs sit between 5.8 and 5.10, many of them several pitches long. A large evergreen in front of the dome is the landmark where most routes begin. Allow about 20 to 30 minutes from the road.

_conflicts.ca_lower_irish_boulders: Stored rock is volcanic rock; one page says fresh granite (https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/lower-irish-boulders-fresh-stone-and-classic-challenges-in-conejo), the Conejo Boulders page says breccia (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/110428197/conejo-boulders).
